newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht seen still cautious on finance worries.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht seen still cautious on finance worries.

text.p: Improved confidence helped the baht weather Thailand's recent financial crisis, but analysts said the currency was likely to trade cautiously in the near term as investors remained wary of fallout from the turmoil.
The currency remained calm through a stock market plunge this month amid fears about the health of Thailand's finance sector.
The Bank of Thailand's firm resolve to defend the baht was effective during the crisis and was expected to make speculators cautious of attacking the currency, analysts said.

"The baht is quite reasonably stable with a little jitter from time to time. But in general terms compared to last month, March has shown much more stability," James Roe, treasury manager at Chase Manhattan Bank NA, said.
The baht was heavily offloaded in February amid speculation that it would be devalued to help cure Thailand's slow export growth and large current account deficit, analysts said.

Analysts have estimated that the central bank, which has repeatedly ruled out a baht devaluation, likely spent billions of dollars to defend the baht between December and Feburary amid the rumours of an impending devaluation.
They said the central bank's intervention in offshore markets had proved its ability to defend the currency and cautioned speculators against a renewed assault.
"They (BOT) have proved themselves in their intervention and action which calmed the market at this time," Roe said.
But investors are expected to remain wary as they watch for further developments in the Thai financial sector.

Analysts said foreign investors were still concerned about the health of most finance companies which had been hit by a bearish stock market and large non-performing loans made mainly to the property sector.

In a revamp of the financial sector, the Bank of Thailand this month ordered 10 weakened finance companies to immediately increase their capital and told all banks and finance companies to raise provisions for substandard loans.
But analysts said the central bank's move to bolster finance companies lifted investors' confidence in the currency at the time.

Alan Erskine, regional market strategist at Citibank Corp in Singapore, said signs of improving economic conditions like an export recovery, declining imports and a low inflation rate also showed that the baht was fairly valued at its current level.
The baht on Friday closed at 25.966/25.969 to the dollar.
Analysts expected the baht to trade in a narrow range in the near term.

"One thing to fear is if the U.S. dollar will strengthen again especially against the yen. If this coincides with more reports of the financial sector weakness, that would provoke new pressure (on the baht)," Erskine said.
